title: Chai Spice Vanilla Cupcakes
shortDescription: Dairy-free chai spice vanilla cupcakes take 25 minutes to prep and bake in 18 minutes, with real brewed chai in the batter.
description: These cupcakes get their flavor from a strong chai tea brewed right into the milk. I steep the tea bags hot, let them cool, then use that liquid in the batter so every bite tastes like a warm mug of chai. The crumb stays soft and dairy-free thanks to oat milk and a neutral oil instead of butter. Cinnamon, cardamom, ginger and clove show up twice, once in the cake and again in the frosting, so the spice does not fade after baking. I tested this batch in my own kitchen on a cold afternoon and the whole house smelled like a coffee shop. The frosting is a dairy-free buttercream warmed up with the same spice blend, piped tall for that bakery look. This recipe works for fall gatherings, holiday tables or anytime you want a cozy flavor without dairy. It also freezes well unfrosted if you want to bake ahead.
ingredients: 1 cup oat milk, warmed but not boiling
3 black tea chai bags (or 2 tbsp loose chai tea)
2 cups dairy-free powdered sugar buttercream (vegan butter, powdered sugar, vanilla)
Pinch ground cardamom and ginger (for frosting)
instructions: Heat the oat milk until steaming, then pour over the chai tea bags. Steep for 8 minutes, squeeze out the bags, and let the milk cool to room temperature.
Preheat your oven to 350°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, cardamom, ginger and cloves.
In a large bowl, whisk the oil and sugar together for 1 minute until combined.
Add the eggs one at a time, whisking well after each, then whisk in the vanilla.
Add the dry ingredients in two batches, alternating with the cooled chai milk. Mix just until no streaks of flour remain.
Divide the batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool the cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move them to a wire rack to cool completely.
Beat the dairy-free buttercream with the extra cinnamon, cardamom and ginger until smooth and warm in color.
Pipe the frosting high on each cooled cupcake using a large star tip.
tips: Steep the chai tea strong. A weak brew gets lost once it mixes with the other ingredients.
Let the chai milk cool fully before adding it to the batter, or it can scramble the eggs later in the mix.
If you like a stronger spice kick, add an extra pinch of ground cloves to the frosting only, since cloves can turn bitter in large amounts.
These cupcakes taste even better the next day, once the spice flavor settles into the crumb.

faq.question: Can I use chai tea bags instead of loose tea for this recipe?
faq.answer: Yes, tea bags work fine and are easier to measure. Use 3 bags steeped for 8 minutes in the warm oat milk for a strong flavor.

faq.question: What dairy-free milk works best for the chai infusion?
faq.answer: Oat milk gives the creamiest texture and blends well with the spices. Soy milk also works if you want a bit more protein in the batter.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost them the day you plan to serve.

faq.question: Is this recipe vegan as well as dairy-free?
faq.answer: Not as written, since it uses eggs. Swap in 2 flax eggs and a vegan buttercream if you need a fully vegan version.

conclusion: These chai spice cupcakes bring a cozy, spiced cup of tea into cake form without any dairy. Brew the chai strong, cool it fully, and the rest of the recipe comes together like a standard vanilla cupcake.
